entries.applies_when: The assignment's level is between_unit, declared or inferred (registry.md, Terms).

availability.condition: The declaration has no assignment block.

constant.template: '{column}' is constant within each of the {units} levels of '{unit}', to which it was assigned between units, a level that is {level}.

mixed.template: '{column}' takes more than one value within {mixed} of the {units} levels of '{unit}', the unit to which it was assigned between units, a level that is {level}. Check these levels for data errors or contamination before the analysis.

agreement.definition: The share of a level's rows that the most frequent value of the assigned column must cover for the level to count as constant, when the level of the assignment is inferred (registry.md, Terms).

sources.citation: 02-decisions.md, Q4. A rule that required 99% agreement within clusters recovered the school level in 99.3 to 100% of 2,000 replicates with up to 0.5% of rows miscoded.

remedies.description: Check the assignment records of the units with mixed values, and correct the data or declare the assignment at the level at which it varies.

level_source.definition: declared when the assignment declares its level, and inferred_from_the_data when its level is inferred (registry.md, Terms).

mixed_units.definition: The number of those levels in which the assigned column takes more than one value.

units.definition: The number of levels of the assignment unit, labelled as the declaration defines its labels, in the rows of the design sample in which the assigned column is not missing.

entries.summary: For a variable assigned between units, checks that it takes one value within each level of the unit to which it was assigned. When the declaration does not state the level of the assignment, the level is inferred from the data with the tolerance of 02-decisions.md (Q4), and the check applies only when it is inferred as between_unit, so that a crossover assignment is not reported as mixed. A unit with mixed values points to a data error or to contamination between arms, which must be resolved before the analysis.
entries.title: Assignment constant within its unit

entries.applies_when: The assignment's level is between_unit, declared or inferred (registry.md, Terms), and some level of the unit has at least two rows in the design sample.

availability.condition: The declaration has no assignment block.

blocks_missing.template: The assignment of '{column}' was blocked by {blocks}, which the formula does not include. '{unit}', to which '{column}' was assigned at a level between units that is {level}, leaves {df} degrees of freedom between its {units} levels after the fixed effects.

design_df.template: '{unit}', the unit to which '{column}' was assigned at a level between units that is {level}, has {units} levels and leaves {df} degrees of freedom between them after the fixed effects.

no_df.template: No degrees of freedom remain between the {units} levels of '{unit}', the unit to which '{column}' was assigned at a level between units that is {level}, after the fixed effects, so the effect of '{column}' cannot be compared with variation between units.

agreement.definition: The share of a level's rows that the most frequent value of the assigned column must cover for the level to count as constant, when the level of the assignment is inferred (registry.md, Terms).

sources.citation: 02-decisions.md, Q4. A rule that required 99% agreement within clusters recovered the school level in 99.3 to 100% of 2,000 replicates with up to 0.5% of rows miscoded.

remedies.description: Add the blocking factors of the assignment to the fixed part.

design_df.definition: The number of indicator columns of the levels of the unit, in level order, that the sequential rule keeps when it is applied to the fixed-effects columns followed by the indicator columns.

level_source.definition: declared when the assignment declares its level, and inferred_from_the_data when its level is inferred (registry.md, Terms).

missing_blocks.definition: The declared blocks of the assignment whose label columns appear neither in the fixed part nor in a grouping factor of the IR, in declared order.

units.definition: The number of levels of the assignment unit in the design sample.

entries.summary: For a variable assigned between units, counts the degrees of freedom between the levels of the assignment unit that remain after the fixed effects, the number of assigned units minus the unit-level fixed parameters computed by rank. The information on an effect assigned to units grows with this number rather than with the number of rows. The check also names declared blocking units that the formula leaves out, since blocking factors used in the assignment belong in the fixed part.
entries.title: Design degrees of freedom of an assignment

entries.applies_when: The assignment is randomised, its level is between_unit, declared or inferred (registry.md, Terms), and some level of the unit has at least two rows in the design sample.

availability.condition: The declaration has no assignment block.

unit_missing.template: '{column}' was randomised by '{unit}', at a level between units that is {level}, but no grouping factor of the model matches the {units} levels of '{unit}'. Grouping factors at higher levels ({coarser}) do not account for the dependence between rows of one '{unit}'. Add a random intercept for '{unit}', analyse '{unit}' means or use cluster-robust inference at that level.

unit_present.template: A grouping factor of the model matches '{unit}', the unit by which '{column}' was randomised, at a level between units that is {level}.

agreement.definition: The share of a level's rows that the most frequent value of the assigned column must cover for the level to count as constant, when the level of the assignment is inferred (registry.md, Terms).

sources.citation: 02-decisions.md, Q4. A rule that required 99% agreement within clusters recovered the school level in 99.3 to 100% of 2,000 replicates with up to 0.5% of rows miscoded.

references.citation: Pustejovsky, J. E., & Tipton, E. (2018). Small-sample methods for cluster-robust variance estimation and hypothesis testing in fixed effects models. Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, 36(4), 672-683.

remedies.description: Add a random intercept for the randomisation unit.
Analyse means at the level of the randomisation unit, which keeps the unit as the unit of inference.
Use cluster-robust standard errors with the CR2 small-sample correction, clustered on the randomisation unit, which the R package offers for nested designs through clubSandwich.

coarser_factors.definition: The grouping factors of the IR, other than one that matches the unit, each of whose levels contains whole levels of the unit, in the order in which they first arise in the IR.

coverage.definition: present when some grouping factor of the IR divides the design sample into the same groups as the levels of the unit, and absent otherwise.

level_source.definition: declared when the assignment declares its level, and inferred_from_the_data when its level is inferred (registry.md, Terms).

units.definition: The number of levels of the assignment unit in the design sample.

entries.summary: For a variable randomised between units, checks that a grouping factor of the model matches the randomisation unit. Leaving the randomised level out of the random part understates the uncertainty of the treatment effect, and a higher level alone never makes up for it. In a review simulation with 4 schools, 6 classes each and randomisation by class, a model with a school intercept only rejected a true null in 31.7% of replicates at a nominal 5%, against 1.3% when class was included (01-design-review.md).
entries.title: Randomisation unit in the random part

entries.applies_when: The term is a main effect, and the fixed part has at least two main-effect terms.

high.template: '{term}' has a generalised variance inflation factor of {gvif}, or {per_df} per degree of freedom, at or above {threshold}, so the design estimates its coefficients with much less precision than uncorrelated predictors would allow.

low.template: '{term}' has a generalised variance inflation factor of {gvif}, or {per_df} per degree of freedom.

moderate.template: '{term}' has a generalised variance inflation factor of {gvif}, or {per_df} per degree of freedom, at or above {threshold}.

references.citation: Fox, J., & Monette, G. (1992). Generalized collinearity diagnostics. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 87(417), 178-183.

remedies.description: Combine collinear predictors into one measure, or remove those that the estimand does not need.
Keep the predictors that the estimand needs and report the wider intervals that the collinearity implies.

df.definition: The number of columns of this term that the sequential rule keeps when it is applied to the intercept followed by the columns of the main-effect terms, as for gvif.

gvif.definition: det(R_TT) det(R_OO) / det(R), where R is the matrix of Pearson correlations, over the rows of the design sample, between the columns of the main-effect terms that the sequential rule keeps when it is applied to the intercept followed by these columns, T are the columns of this term, O the other columns and the determinant of an empty matrix is 1. It is absent when df is 0.

gvif_per_df.definition: gvif raised to the power 1/df, which equals the variance inflation factor for a term with one column. It is absent when df is 0.

entries.summary: Computes the generalised variance inflation factor of each main-effect term from the fixed-effects matrix, which does not change with the coding of a factor's contrasts. Interaction terms are left out, because the factor of a lower-order term in a model with its interactions depends on the centring of the variables it interacts with. The check reads the design only and ignores the covariance of the fitted model, so it describes the design rather than the standard errors of a fit.

high.rationale: The upper value of the same rule of thumb.

sources.citation: James, G., Witten, D., Hastie, T., & Tibshirani, R. (2013). An introduction to statistical learning: With applications in R. Springer.

moderate.rationale: A widely quoted rule of thumb treats a variance inflation factor above 5 or 10 as a problematic amount of collinearity. Comparing the factor per degree of freedom with it extends the rule to terms with several columns.

sources.citation: James, G., Witten, D., Hastie, T., & Tibshirani, R. (2013). An introduction to statistical learning: With applications in R. Springer.
Fox, J., & Monette, G. (1992). Generalized collinearity diagnostics. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 87(417), 178-183.

entries.title: Collinearity of a fixed term

focal.template: The fixed-effects columns {dropped} depend on earlier columns and are dropped, which affects the focal terms among {terms}. Their coefficients then refer to a subset that depends on the design. Combinations of factor levels without rows: {empty}.

full_rank.template: The {columns} fixed-effects columns are linearly independent.

nonfocal.template: The fixed-effects columns {dropped} depend on earlier columns and are dropped. They belong to {terms}, none of them focal. Combinations of factor levels without rows: {empty}.

references.citation: ir.md, the sequential rule for dropping aliased columns

remedies.description: Recode the factors of an incomplete interaction as one factor of the observed cells, or collapse levels, and state the estimands for the observed cells.
Remove a term whose columns the others already span.

columns.definition: The number of fixed-effects columns of the IR, the intercept included.

dropped_columns.definition: The columns that the sequential rule drops, named as the IR names them, in column order.

dropped_terms.definition: The terms that own a dropped column, in term order.

empty_cells.definition: The number of combinations of levels that have no row in the design sample, summed over the interaction terms whose factors are all categorical, with the levels of each factor that occur in the design sample.

focal_dropped.definition: Whether a dropped column belongs to a focal term.

kept.definition: The number of columns that the sequential rule keeps, the rank of the fixed-effects matrix.

entries.summary: Applies the sequential rule of ir.md to the fixed-effects columns, which drops the later member of each dependent set in column order as lme4 does, and reports the dropped columns, the terms they belong to and the empty cells of interactions between factors. A greedy pivoted QR can drop different columns, so both packages use the sequential rule. When cells are empty, the coefficients of the affected terms refer to a subset that depends on the design.
entries.title: Rank deficiency of the fixed effects

entries.applies_when: At least one fixed-effects column other than the intercept takes a value other than 0 and 1 in the design sample.

rules.condition: sd_ratio exceeds ratio, sd_largest exceeds high or sd_smallest is below low.

disparate.template: The standard deviations of {columns} differ by a factor of {ratio}, or one of them lies outside 0.001 to 1000, which makes lme4 warn that the predictors are on very different scales. Centre and scale these columns outside the formula with stored constants.

similar.template: The standard deviations of {columns} differ by a factor of {ratio} at most.

remedies.description: Centre and scale the columns outside the formula with stored constants, and report coefficients transformed back to the original units.

condition_number.definition: The ratio of the largest to the smallest singular value of the matrix of the fixed-effects columns that the sequential rule keeps, each scaled to unit Euclidean length.

scaled_columns.definition: The fixed-effects columns, other than the intercept, that take a value other than 0 and 1 in the design sample, in column order.

sd_largest.definition: The largest standard deviation of those columns, with denominator n - 1, where n is the number of rows of the design sample.

sd_ratio.definition: sd_largest divided by sd_smallest, absent when sd_smallest is 0.

sd_smallest.definition: The smallest of those standard deviations.

entries.summary: Anticipates lme4's warning that predictors are on very different scales, which it gives when the standard deviations of the fixed-effects columns that are not all 0 or 1 differ by a factor above 1000, or when one of them lies above 1000 or below 0.001. The warning concerns the units of the columns, so the check also reports the condition number of the fixed-effects matrix with columns scaled to unit length, which measures near-dependence between the columns and which a change of units does not alter.

high.rationale: The standard deviation above which lme4 warns.

sources.citation: lme4 2.1-1, the check of the scales of the fixed-effects columns that the check.scaleX setting of lmerControl() controls, as the review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md, L2-13) describes it.

low.rationale: The standard deviation below which lme4 warns.

sources.citation: lme4 2.1-1, the check of the scales of the fixed-effects columns that the check.scaleX setting of lmerControl() controls, as the review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md, L2-13) describes it.

ratio.rationale: The ratio of standard deviations above which lme4 warns.

sources.citation: lme4 2.1-1, the check of the scales of the fixed-effects columns that the check.scaleX setting of lmerControl() controls, as the review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md, L2-13) describes it.

entries.title: Scales of the fixed-effects columns

budget.template: '{factor}' has {levels} levels and {budget} degrees of freedom between levels after the fixed effects.

no_budget.template: No degrees of freedom between levels of '{factor}' remain after the fixed effects, since {terms} use up its {levels} levels, so the variance of its random intercept is not identified under REML.

references.citation: Review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md), L1-10, with the verifier's correction that d equals J minus the dimension of the intersection of the column spaces of X and Z, computed by rank.

remedies.description: Remove fixed effects that are constant within the levels of the factor, or treat the factor as a fixed effect without a random intercept.

budget.definition: The number of indicator columns of the factor, one for each level in level order, that the sequential rule keeps when it is applied to the fixed-effects columns followed by the indicator columns.

consuming_terms.definition: The fixed terms, the intercept included, whose removal from the fixed-effects columns raises budget, in term order.

levels.definition: The number of levels of the factor in the design sample.

entries.summary: Counts the independent contrasts between the levels of a grouping factor that remain after the fixed effects, d = rank([X, Z]) - rank(X) with Z the indicator matrix of the factor. When it is 0, as when the factor is also a fixed effect or its levels are used up by level-constant covariates, the variance of its random intercept is not identified under REML. In balanced designs it equals the denominator degrees of freedom for effects that are constant within levels. It is computed by rank, never by counting columns, because columns that vary within levels can combine into a direction that does not.
entries.title: Degrees of freedom between the levels of a grouping factor

availability.condition: Z has more than max_z_columns columns.

identified.template: The design identifies all {parameters} covariance parameters, the residual variance included.

necessary_only.template: The bases of the {parameters} covariance parameters are linearly independent on the latent scale, which is necessary for identification in this family but does not establish it.

not_identified.template: The design does not identify the covariance parameters of the random part: the Gram matrix of their bases has rank {rank} for {parameters} parameters, and {null} cannot be separated from each other.

max_z_columns.definition: The largest number of columns of Z for which the check runs, which keeps the dense matrix W below 200 MB.

sources.citation: Set by this project for registry 0.1.0.

null_loading.definition: The share of the largest square root of a diagonal element of the projector at or above which a parameter belongs to the confounded set.

sources.citation: Set by this project for registry 0.1.0.

rank_tolerance.definition: The relative tolerance below which an eigenvalue of the scaled Gram matrix, or a diagonal element of the Gram matrix relative to the largest, counts as zero.

sources.citation: Set by this project for registry 0.1.0. Exactly confounded parameters give eigenvalues at the level of rounding error, near 1e-16, far below it.

references.citation: Review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md), L1-06, with the verifier's corrections: the bases are projected for Gaussian models and unprojected on the latent scale for other families, and the raw condition number is not scale-free.

remedies.description: Remove or merge the random terms whose parameters are confounded, starting with those named, or change a coding that makes uncorrelated terms unidentified.

null_parameters.definition: The vanishing parameters, followed by the parameters k of C with sqrt(d_k) at least null_loading times the largest sqrt(d_j), where d_k is the sum of v_ik squared over an orthonormal basis v_1, ..., v_r of the eigenvectors of C whose eigenvalues are at or below rank_tolerance, the diagonal of the projector onto their span. The projector does not depend on the basis chosen, so that every confounded parameter is named however the eigenvalues at rounding level are ordered. The list is empty when no eigenvalue is at or below rank_tolerance. Parameters are named as the IR names them, in their IR order.

parameters.definition: The number of covariance parameters of the random terms, a variance for each column of a term and a covariance for each pair of columns of a term that estimates correlations, plus 1 for the residual variance when the family class is gaussian.

rank.definition: parameters minus the number of vanishing parameters minus the number of eigenvalues of C at or below rank_tolerance. For the gaussian family class, let X be the fixed-effects columns that the sequential rule keeps, P = I - X(X'X)^-1 X', Z the random-effects matrix of the IR on the design sample and W = Z'PZ. For other family classes, W = Z'Z and the residual is left out. Each covariance parameter k has a symmetric basis matrix A_k over the columns of Z: 1 at the diagonal position of the column in every level of the term's factor for a variance, and 1 at the two positions of the pair of columns in every level for a covariance. The Gram matrix M has M_kl = tr(A_k W A_l W) for covariance parameters, M_ks = tr(A_k W) between a covariance parameter and the residual, and M_ss = n - rank(X), with n the number of rows of the design sample. A parameter vanishes when its diagonal element of M is at or below rank_tolerance times the largest diagonal element. C is M restricted to the other parameters and scaled to C_kl = M_kl / sqrt(M_kk M_ll).

smallest_eigenvalue.definition: The smallest eigenvalue of C, a scale-free index of how close the design comes to confounding parameters. It is a heuristic, absent when C is empty.

verdict.definition: not_identified when rank is below parameters, and otherwise identified for the gaussian family class and necessary_condition_met for the other family classes, for which the test covers a necessary condition only.

entries.summary: Tests whether the covariance parameters of the random part can be separated by the design, before any fit. For a Gaussian model whose covariance parameters enter the marginal covariance linearly, the parameters are identified under REML if and only if their REML-projected covariance bases and the projection itself are linearly independent, which the rank of their Gram matrix decides. The rank of Z is the wrong criterion. For other family classes, the check uses the unprojected bases on the latent scale without the residual, which gives a necessary condition only, so the verdict is then necessary_condition_met rather than identified (02-decisions.md, Q3). The space spanned by the eigenvectors of the vanishing eigenvalues names the parameters that the design confounds.
entries.title: Identifiability of the covariance parameters

adequate.template: {informative} of the {levels} levels of '{factor}' vary in every column of '{term}', which has {dimension} random effects for each level.

guaranteed.template: '{term}' has {dimension} random effects for each level of '{factor}', but its {levels} levels support a covariance matrix of rank {bound} at most, so the fit will be singular. A fit reported as non-singular would suggest that the optimiser stopped early.

likely.template: Only {informative} levels of '{factor}' vary in every column of '{term}', no more than its {dimension} random effects for each level, so a singular fit is likely.

references.citation: Review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md), L1-07, with the verifier's condition that the bound J - 1 needs fixed-effect counterparts for the term's columns.

remedies.description: Reduce the term along the plan's ladder, removing correlations before variances and terms that few levels inform before the others.

bound.definition: levels minus 1 when counterparts is true, and levels otherwise.

counterparts.definition: Whether the sequential rule, applied to the fixed-effects columns followed by the term's columns, keeps none of the term's columns.

dimension.definition: The number of columns of the term, which is the number of random effects for each level.

informative_levels.definition: The number of levels in which the term's columns, restricted to the level's rows, have rank equal to dimension by the sequential rule.

levels.definition: The number of levels of the term's grouping factor in the design sample.

entries.summary: Compares the number of levels of a grouping factor with the number of random effects that a term estimates for each level. When the term's columns also appear in the fixed part, J levels support a covariance matrix of rank at most J - 1, and at most J otherwise, so a term whose dimension exceeds this bound gives a singular fit whatever the data, and a fit reported as non-singular then suggests that the optimiser stopped early. Levels in which the term's columns do not all vary inform the covariance only in part, so few informative levels make a singular fit likely.
entries.title: Levels against the dimension of a random term

entries.applies_when: The term's columns are the intercept and columns coded from factors, so that its rows take finitely many patterns.

rules.condition: replicated_cells is 0, the family class is gaussian or other, and columns is 1 or correlated is true.
replicated_cells is 0 and the family class is bernoulli.
replicated_cells is 0 and the family class is gaussian or other.

bernoulli.template: Each combination of a level of '{factor}' and a cell of '{term}' has one row, so '{term}' acts as an observation-level effect, which is not identified under a probit link and only weakly identified under a logit link.

coding_dependent.template: Each combination of a level of '{factor}' and a cell of '{term}' has one row. With uncorrelated random effects, '{term}' is identified only through the restriction that its coding imposes, if at all, and the result changes with the coding.

confounded.template: Each combination of a level of '{factor}' and a cell of '{term}' has one row, so the random effects of '{term}' are confounded with the residual and not identified.

overdispersion.template: Each combination of a level of '{factor}' and a cell of '{term}' has one row, so '{term}' acts as an observation-level effect, which models overdispersion in this family.

replicated.template: {replicated} of the {cells} combinations of a level of '{factor}' and a cell of '{term}' have two or more rows.

references.citation: Review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md), L1-05 and L7-14, with the verifiers' corrections on coding and on families.

remedies.description: Remove the term, whose variance the residual already carries, or reduce it to the components that replicated cells identify.

cells.definition: The number of distinct combinations of a level of the term's grouping factor and a pattern of the term's columns in the design sample, two rows having the same pattern when all the term's columns are equal. Its count class is that of the grouping factor.

columns.definition: The number of columns of the term.

correlated.definition: Whether the term has two or more columns and estimates their correlations.

replicated_cells.definition: The number of those combinations that hold at least two rows.

entries.summary: For a random term whose columns come from factors, checks whether any combination of a level of its grouping factor and a cell of its columns holds more than one row. With one row per combination, as with a subject-by-item intercept in a Latin-square design or one observation per subject and condition, a Gaussian model cannot separate the term from the residual when the term has one column or estimates correlations, and with uncorrelated columns it is identified only through the restriction its coding imposes, if at all. For Bernoulli outcomes the term acts as an observation-level effect, which is not identified under a probit link and weakly identified under a logit link, whereas for binomial outcomes with trials and counts it is an identified overdispersion term.
entries.title: Random effects confounded with the residual

availability.condition: The declaration gives no observation key.

conflicting.template: {conflicting} values of the observation key {key} occur in rows that differ in other columns, and {identical} in identical rows, {rows} rows in all. Each row must have its own key value.

double_import.template: {identical} values of the observation key {key} occur in two or more identical rows, {rows} rows in all, which suggests rows imported twice. Remove the copies at the source.

missing_key.template: {missing} rows have a missing value in the observation key {key}.

unique.template: Every row has its own value of the observation key {key}.

remedies.description: Correct the duplicated or missing key values at the source. The packages never remove rows automatically.

conflicting_keys.definition: The number of duplicated key values whose rows differ in a compared column. The compared columns are those that the IR reads, other than the response and its trials column, and those that the declaration gives a role other than outcome or outcome_derived. Missing values are equal to each other.

duplicate_rows.definition: The number of rows whose key value occurs in another row.

duplicated_keys.definition: The number of distinct values of the key, among rows without a missing key value, that occur in two or more rows. Key values are compared as the table reader returns them, labels after NFC normalisation.

key_columns.definition: The columns of the declared observation key, in the declared order.

missing_key_rows.definition: The number of rows with a missing value in a key column.

rows.definition: The number of rows of the table.

entries.summary: Checks that every row of the table has its own value of the declared observation key. Identical rows are legitimate in trial-level data without a trial index, so duplicates are judged against the key and never against whole rows, and rows are never removed automatically. A key value shared by rows that differ elsewhere is an error in the data, and one shared by identical rows suggests rows imported twice. The check runs on the whole table, before rows with missing values are removed, and compares the columns it may read at T0, which exclude the outcome.
entries.title: Duplicates of the declared observation key

entries.applies_when: The column holds labels: a grouping column, a categorical predictor of the fixed part, a column of the declared observation key or a declared assignment column. The outcome is not read.

distinct.template: No two labels in '{column}' differ only in their Unicode form.

merged.template: {spellings} distinct spellings in '{column}' differ only in their Unicode form and are treated as {labels} labels.

references.citation: conventions.md, Text and Unicode, and 02-decisions.md, cross-cutting conventions

remedies.description: Normalise the labels to NFC in the data source, so that other software reading the data treats them as the analysis does.

labels.definition: The number of distinct NFC forms that those strings share.

spellings.definition: The number of distinct strings of the column in the table that share their NFC form with another distinct string of the column. A string that is not normalisable stands for itself (conventions.md, NFC).

entries.summary: Labels are compared after NFC normalisation (conventions.md, Text and Unicode), so distinct spellings that are canonically equivalent, such as a precomposed and a decomposed accented letter, count as one label. The check reports each column in which such spellings occur, so that the merge is visible rather than silent. It compares no case and no white space.
entries.title: Labels that differ only in Unicode form

entries.applies_when: The declared measurement of the outcome is bounded_score.

availability.condition: The declaration gives no measurement level for the outcome.

rules.condition: floor_share exceeds floor or ceiling_share exceeds ceiling.

at_bounds.template: {floor_share} of the rows are at the lowest possible score and {ceiling_share} at the highest, more than {threshold} at a bound. Consider a binomial or beta-binomial model when the maximum is a number of items, or an item-level model when item responses exist, and report any interaction on both scales.

within_bounds.template: {floor_share} of the rows are at the lowest possible score and {ceiling_share} at the highest.

remedies.description: Model a sum of item scores as binomial or beta-binomial with the maximum as trials, or fit an item-level model when item responses exist.
Report an interaction on both the observed and a latent scale, with a note that it may depend on the scale.

at_ceiling.definition: The number of rows whose outcome equals the upper declared bound, compared by value.

at_floor.definition: The number of rows whose outcome equals the lower declared bound, compared by value.

rows.definition: The number of rows of the analysis sample.

entries.summary: For a score with declared bounds, reports the share of rows of the analysis sample at the lowest and at the highest possible value. A mass at a bound compresses variance, makes residuals heteroscedastic and turns additive effects on a latent scale into interactions on the observed scale. The 15% cut-off is a psychometric reporting convention for floor and ceiling effects, and the check reports it without choosing a model. Shares within design cells relate the outcome to predictors and belong to T2.

ceiling.rationale: More than 15% of respondents at the highest possible score is a common criterion for a ceiling effect.

sources.citation: Terwee, C. B., Bot, S. D. M., de Boer, M. R., van der Windt, D. A. W. M., Knol, D. L., Dekker, J., Bouter, L. M., & de Vet, H. C. W. (2007). Quality criteria were proposed for measurement properties of health status questionnaires. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 60(1), 34-42.

floor.rationale: More than 15% of respondents at the lowest possible score is a common criterion for a floor effect.

sources.citation: Terwee, C. B., Bot, S. D. M., de Boer, M. R., van der Windt, D. A. W. M., Knol, D. L., Dekker, J., Bouter, L. M., & de Vet, H. C. W. (2007). Quality criteria were proposed for measurement properties of health status questionnaires. Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, 60(1), 34-42.

entries.title: Outcome values at the declared bounds

many.template: The outcome is constant within {constant} of the {levels} levels of '{factor}' that have two or more rows ({share}). For a binary outcome, this can push the standard deviation of the random intercept towards very large values, and by-'{factor}' slopes rest on the other levels.

no_levels.template: No level of '{factor}' has two or more rows, so variation within levels cannot be assessed.

none_constant.template: The outcome varies within every level of '{factor}' that has two or more rows.

some.template: The outcome is constant within {constant} of the {levels} levels of '{factor}' that have two or more rows.

remedies.description: Report the share of constant levels with the variance estimates, and treat a very large standard deviation of the random intercept as a consequence of these levels.
Where the design allows, model binary rows as binomial counts per cell with their trials, which gives the same estimates and comparable dispersion statistics.

constant_levels.definition: The number of those levels within which the response vector of ir.md (Response, offsets and weights) takes one value, so that for a binary outcome with a declared event level all the other categories count as one. A categorical outcome without a response vector, such as an ordinal item, is constant in a level when its labels, compared after NFC, take one value there. For the binomial family class, a level is constant when all its rows have no events or all have as many events as trials.

constant_share.definition: constant_levels divided by multi_row_levels, absent when multi_row_levels is 0.

multi_row_levels.definition: The number of levels of the factor with at least two rows in the analysis sample.

entries.summary: Counts the levels of a grouping factor within which the outcome does not vary. For a binary outcome, as with participants at 100% accuracy, such levels contribute almost nothing to their own random slopes, and many of them can push the standard deviation of the random intercept towards very large values. For other outcomes, constant levels point to floor or ceiling effects or to errors in the data. The check reads the outcome by grouping factor only.

any.rationale: One constant level is reported so that its effect on the slopes can be judged.

sources.citation: Set by this project for registry 0.1.0.

many.rationale: A quarter of the levels without variation is taken as many, the point at which the variance estimates rest largely on the other levels. The cut-off is a convention, to be calibrated in the GLMM studies V8 to V10.

sources.citation: Set by this project for registry 0.1.0.
Review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md), L3-20 and L3-03.

entries.title: Levels without outcome variation

availability.condition: The family class is bernoulli, the outcome takes values other than 0 and 1, as numbers or logical values, and the declaration gives no event level.

events.template: The outcome has {events} events and {non_events} non-events, or {per_column} minority events per fixed-effects column. In {without} of the {levels} levels of '{factor}' one of the two classes is absent, and the median level has {median} minority events.

events.definition: The number of events in the analysis sample: rows whose value of the response vector of ir.md (Response, offsets and weights) is 1 for the bernoulli family class, and the sum of the event counts for the binomial family class.

events_per_column.definition: The smaller of events and non-events divided by the statistic kept of design.rank_deficiency, the number of fixed-effects columns that the sequential rule keeps on the design sample, so that the check reads no predictor. It is absent when kept is 0.

levels.definition: The number of levels of the factor in the analysis sample.

levels_without_minority.definition: The number of levels in which the smaller of the level's events and non-events is 0.

median_minority.definition: The level minority count at position ceil(J/2) when the smaller of each level's events and non-events are sorted in increasing order, with J the number of levels.

non_events.definition: The number of rows, or of trials for the binomial family class, minus events.

entries.summary: For binary and binomial outcomes, the information about effects grows with the number of events in the minority class rather than with the number of rows. The check reports the events and non-events in the analysis sample, the minority count in each level of a grouping factor and the minority events per fixed-effects column, as an index without a cut-off. It reads the outcome by grouping factor only.
entries.title: Minority events of a binary outcome

availability.condition: In R, lpSolveAPI is not installed. In Python, scipy provides the solver.
The family class is bernoulli, the outcome takes values other than 0 and 1, as numbers or logical values, and the declaration gives no event level.

complete.template: The fixed effects separate the events from the non-events completely, through {columns}, so the estimates of these coefficients diverge and their Wald statistics are unreliable.

none.template: The fixed effects do not separate the events from the non-events.

quasi.template: The fixed effects separate the events from the non-events quasi-completely, through {columns}, so the estimates of these coefficients diverge and their Wald statistics are unreliable.

bound_tolerance.definition: The absolute difference within which the coefficient bounds and the optimum from the two packages agree (02-decisions.md, Q2, and conventions.md, Comparison across languages).

sources.citation: 02-decisions.md, Q2

separation_tolerance.definition: The value above which an optimum of the linear programs, computed on columns scaled to a largest absolute value of 1, indicates separation.

sources.citation: Set by this project for registry 0.1.0, well above the default feasibility tolerances of lpSolve and of HiGHS in scipy.

references.citation: Albert, A., & Anderson, J. A. (1984). On the existence of maximum likelihood estimates in logistic regression models. Biometrika, 71(1), 1-10.
Konis, K. (2007). Linear programming algorithms for detecting separated data in binary logistic regression models [Doctoral thesis, University of Oxford]. Oxford University Research Archive.

remedies.description: Merge sparse levels or remove the interaction that creates the separation, if this was declared as a contingency before the outcome was seen.
Use penalised or Bayesian estimation with weakly informative priors on the fixed effects, and report likelihood-ratio tests or profile intervals for the affected terms rather than Wald tests.

bounds.definition: For each kept column in column order, the smallest and the largest value of b_j over the optimal face of the first program, the set of b that meets its constraints with a sum of s x'b of at least v1 minus separation_tolerance, as the pairs (smallest, largest) laid out in one list. Both packages compare these values within bound_tolerance.

columns_involved.definition: The kept columns whose largest value in bounds is above separation_tolerance or whose smallest value is below minus separation_tolerance, in column order.

optimum.definition: v1, the optimum of the first linear program, which the two packages compare within bound_tolerance, as they compare bounds.

verdict.definition: Let X be the fixed-effects columns of the analysis sample that the sequential rule keeps, each divided by its largest absolute value. Each row gives one observation with sign s = 1 when it is an event and s = -1 otherwise. For the binomial family class, a row with k events of n trials gives an observation with s = 1 when k is above 0 and one with s = -1 when k is below n. The first linear program maximises the sum over observations of s x'b subject to s x'b >= 0 for every observation and -1 <= b_j <= 1 for every coefficient, with optimum v1. The second maximises t subject to s x'b >= t for every observation, the same bounds on b and t <= 1, with optimum v2. The verdict is complete when v2 is above separation_tolerance, quasi when v1 is above separation_tolerance, and none otherwise.

entries.summary: Tests by linear programming whether the fixed-effects columns separate the events from the non-events completely or quasi-completely, in which case the maximum-likelihood estimates of the fixed effects diverge, with or without random effects. An all-0 or all-1 cell is neither necessary nor sufficient for separation, which depends only on the column space of the fixed effects and so does not change with the coding. Because different solver settings can return different optimal vertices, the check reports the verdict with the range of each coefficient over the optimal face, which both packages compare within bound_tolerance. The check relates the outcome to the predictors, so Stream B runs it only in its exploratory mode (02-decisions.md, Q2 and Q3).
entries.title: Separation of a binary outcome by the fixed effects

zeros.template: {share} of the {rows} counts are 0, and every count is 0 in {all_zero} of the {levels} levels of '{factor}'. Many zeros alone do not indicate zero inflation in a model with random effects.

all_zero_levels.definition: The number of levels in which every count is 0.

levels.definition: The number of levels of the factor in the analysis sample.

rows.definition: The number of rows of the analysis sample.

zeros.definition: The number of rows whose outcome is 0.

entries.summary: Reports the share of zeros of a count outcome in the analysis sample and the levels of each grouping factor in which every count is 0. Many zeros do not by themselves indicate zero inflation, because random intercepts already make counts zero-heavy, and a comparison with a marginal Poisson distribution is invalid with clustering, so the check grades no finding.
entries.title: Zeros of a count outcome

complete.template: All {raw} rows are complete in the columns that the model reads.

reference_emptied.template: The reference level of {factors} has no rows left after {dropped} of {raw} rows with missing values leave the design sample, so the coefficients of these factors no longer compare with the declared reference level.

rows_dropped.template: {dropped} of {raw} rows have a missing value in {columns} and leave the design sample. Factors that lose a level: {emptied}. Grouping factors that lose levels: {losing}. Grouping factors with new singletons: {singletons}.

references.citation: Review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md), L1-09, L2-04 and L2-21.

remedies.description: Declare a reference level that remains in the analysis sample, and state the estimands for the analysis sample.
If missingness may depend on observed variables, consider an analysis that uses the incomplete rows, such as multiple imputation with an imputation model that respects the clustering.

emptied_factors.definition: The categorical predictors of the fixed part with a level that occurs in the table but not in the design sample, in code-point order of their names.

factors_losing_levels.definition: The grouping factors with a level that occurs in the table, in a row in which the factor's own columns are not missing, but not in the design sample, in the order in which they first arise in the IR.

incomplete_columns.definition: The columns that the IR reads, other than the response and its trials column, and the sample columns of the IR that have a missing value in at least one row of the table, in code-point order of their names.

new_singletons.definition: The grouping factors with a level that has one row in the design sample and more than one in the table, in the order in which they first arise in the IR.

reference_emptied.definition: The categorical predictors whose reference level, as ir.md fixes it, occurs in the table but not in the design sample, in code-point order of their names.

rows_kept.definition: The number of rows of the design sample.

rows_raw.definition: The number of rows of the table as read.

entries.summary: Every audit runs on the analysis sample, and this check reports how it differs from the raw table: the rows that a missing value removes, the levels of factors that lose all their rows and the grouping factors whose levels disappear or become singletons. A level emptied in this way can change the reference level of a factor without notice or leave a column of zeros. As a T0 check, it compares the raw table with the design sample and does not read the outcome.
entries.title: Differences between the raw data and the analysis sample

aliased.template: '{first}' and '{second}' divide the design sample into the same groups, so their random effects on the same columns are aliased and only the sum of their variances is identified. Keep one of the two factors.

distinct.template: '{first}' and '{second}' divide the design sample into different groups, and neither is nested in the other.

nested.template: {informative} of the {levels} levels of {coarser} contain two or more levels of {finer}, with {rows} rows. The variance of {finer} separate from that of {coarser} rests on these levels alone.

references.citation: Review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md), L1-02: with identical partitions the REML-projected covariance bases have rank 2 of 3, with the null direction of the difference of the two variances.

remedies.description: Remove the random terms of one of the two factors, since the data cannot separate their variances.

coarser.definition: The coarser factor when partition is first_finer or second_finer, and no factor otherwise.

coarser_levels.definition: The number of levels of the coarser factor, and 0 when there is none.

finer.definition: The finer factor when partition is first_finer or second_finer, and no factor otherwise.

informative_levels.definition: The number of levels of the coarser factor that contain at least two levels of the finer factor, and 0 when there is no coarser factor. Its count class is that of the coarser factor.

informative_rows.definition: The number of rows of the design sample in the levels that informative_levels counts.

partition.definition: identical when every level of each factor occurs with exactly one level of the other in the design sample, first_finer when every level of the first occurs with exactly one level of the second but not conversely, second_finer in the reverse case, and other otherwise.

entries.summary: Two grouping factors that divide the design sample into the same groups give random effects with identical covariance bases, so only the sum of their variances is identified, as with one class per school or a session identifier that equals the subject identifier after rows are dropped. The comparison uses the partitions and ignores the labels. For a factor nested in another, the check reports how many levels of the coarser factor contain more than one level of the finer factor, since the variance of the finer factor rests on those levels alone.
entries.title: Grouping factors with identical partitions

rules.condition: levels equals rows and the family class is gaussian or other.
levels equals rows and the family class is bernoulli.
levels equals rows and the family class is binomial or poisson.

observation_level.template: Every level of '{factor}' has one row, so its random intercept is an observation-level effect, which models overdispersion in this family.

one_row_bernoulli.template: Every level of '{factor}' has one row, so its random intercept is an observation-level effect, which a binary outcome does not identify under a probit link and identifies only weakly under a logit link.

one_row_per_level.template: Every level of '{factor}' has one row, so its random intercept duplicates the residual and the two variances are not separately identified.

sizes.template: '{factor}' has {levels} levels with {rows} rows. Level sizes range from {smallest} to {largest}, with quartiles {lower} and {upper} and median {median}, and {singletons} levels have one row, which are kept.

references.citation: Review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md), L1-02, L1-09 and L1-19.

remedies.description: Remove the random terms of the factor, whose variance the residual already carries in this family.

effective_size.definition: The effective level size n0 = (N - S/N)/(J - 1), where S is the sum of the squared level sizes, for which the expected between-level mean square of a one-way layout is the residual variance plus n0 times the variance of the factor. It is absent when J is 1.

largest.definition: The largest number of rows in a level.

levels.definition: The number of levels of the factor in the design sample, J.

lower_quartile.definition: The level size at position ceil(J/4) when the level sizes are sorted in increasing order and counted from 1.

median.definition: The level size at position ceil(J/2) in the same order.

rows.definition: The number of rows of the design sample, N.

singletons.definition: The number of levels with one row.

smallest.definition: The smallest number of rows in a level.

upper_quartile.definition: The level size at position ceil(3J/4) in the same order.

entries.summary: Reports the distribution of the rows of the design sample over the levels of a grouping factor, with the singletons, which are kept, and the effective level size of an unbalanced one-way layout. Only levels with two or more rows separate the variance of the factor from the residual variance. A factor with one row per level duplicates the residual in a Gaussian model, whereas for counts and binomial outcomes with trials it is an observation-level random effect, a standard term for overdispersion.
entries.title: Level sizes of a grouping factor

entries.applies_when: For the pair, the statistic partition of structure.aliased_factors is other.

rules.condition: components is at least 2 and between_component_terms is not empty.

confounded.template: '{first}' and '{second}' form {components} disconnected groups of levels, and {terms} do not vary within these groups, so their effects rest only on the differences between the groups.

connected.template: '{first}' and '{second}' are connected: rows link every level to every other level.

disconnected.template: '{first}' and '{second}' form {components} disconnected groups of levels, so their random effects are compared only within each group.

remedies.description: Report the effects of terms that are constant within the groups as comparisons between the groups, or collect data that link the groups.

between_component_terms.definition: The fixed terms other than the intercept, in term order, whose columns, restricted to the rows of each component, have rank 0 by the sequential rule after the component's first row is subtracted from every row, in every component.

components.definition: The number of connected components of the graph whose vertices are the levels of the two factors and whose edges join two levels that occur together in a row of the design sample.

entries.summary: For two grouping factors that neither nest nor share a partition, such as subjects and items, counts the connected groups of levels that rows link together. In a disconnected design, the two sets of random effects are compared only within each group, and a fixed term that is constant within every group is estimated only from the differences between the groups.
entries.title: Connectivity of two crossed grouping factors

entries.applies_when: For the pair, the statistic declared of structure.label_incidence is none, its statistic composite is false and its relation is crossed or partially_crossed.

no_attribute.template: No column is constant within the units that the repeated labels of {labels_column} denote, so the data give no evidence on whether a label denotes one unit across the levels of {context_column}. Declare the scope of the labels.

no_change.template: None of the {shared} labels of {labels_column} that occur with several levels of {context_column} changes any of the attributes {attributes}, which is consistent with labels that each denote one unit. Declare the scope of the labels to confirm it.

reuse_likely.template: For {share} of the {shared} labels of {labels_column} that occur with several levels of {context_column}, the attribute {attribute} changes between those levels, so these labels probably denote different units. The model treats each label as one unit. Declare the scope of the labels, and nest {labels_column} in {context_column} if the labels are reused.

some_change.template: For {changing} of the {shared} labels of {labels_column} that occur with several levels of {context_column}, the attribute {attribute} changes between those levels. Check these units and declare the scope of the labels.

remedies.description: Declare the two units with nested_in and id_scope, or as a crossing, so that the relation no longer rests on the labels alone.
If the labels are reused within each level of the context column, write the random term with '/' so that the IR builds a grouping factor whose levels are unique across the data.

attributes.definition: The candidate attributes, in code-point order of their names. They are the columns of the design sample that the IR reads, other than the response, its trials column and the two columns of the pair, and the columns that the declaration gives a role other than outcome or outcome_derived, that are constant within every combination of a label of the labels column and a label of the context column but not within every label of the context column. Constancy compares the values as the table reader returns them, with missing values equal to each other.

changing_attribute.definition: The candidate attribute that gives changing_labels, the first in code-point order of their names on a tie, and no column when there is no candidate attribute.

changing_labels.definition: The largest number, over the candidate attributes, of shared labels for which the attribute takes more than one value across the labels of the context column with which they occur.

context_column.definition: The other column of the pair in the reported direction.

labels_column.definition: The column whose repeated labels the evidence concerns. The statistics below are computed for each direction in which labels of one column, the labels column, occur with more than one label of the other, the context column. The direction with the larger changing_share is reported, and on a tie the direction whose labels column is the first column.

shared_labels.definition: The number of labels of the labels column that occur with more than one label of the context column.

entries.summary: When labels of one grouping column occur with several labels of another and the declaration states no relation between the two units, the check reports outcome-free evidence on whether a repeated label denotes one unit or several: whether attributes that are fixed for a unit keep their value across the levels of the other column. In mlmRev's Exam data, 269 of 322 shared student labels change sex across schools, whereas in a crossed psycholinguistic dataset none of 600 items changes its frequency or length (02-decisions.md, Q4). The evidence informs a declaration and never decides the coding.

any_change.rationale: One shared label whose fixed attribute changes shows that at least one repeated label does not denote a single unit with consistent data.

sources.citation: Set by this project for registry 0.1.0.

most_change.rationale: When at least half of the shared labels change an attribute that is fixed for a unit, the labels most probably denote different units in different contexts, as in the Exam data.

sources.citation: Set by this project for registry 0.1.0, to be replaced by a validated rule.
02-decisions.md, Q4

entries.title: Evidence on the scope of repeated labels

rules.condition: declared is nested_within_parent, composite is false and inner_in_several is above 0.
declared is nested_global and inner_in_several is above 0.
declared is nested_mobile, composite is true and inner_in_several is above 0.
declared is crossed and composite is true.

crossed_split.template: The declaration states that '{first}' and '{second}' are crossed, so that a label shared between levels of one denotes one unit, but the model combines the two columns into one grouping factor and splits such units.

labels_change_parent.template: {count} labels of {inner} occur under more than one level of {outer}, although the declaration states that each unit stays in one level of {outer} and that its label is unique across the data.

merged_units.template: {count} labels of {inner} occur under more than one level of {outer}. The declaration states that these labels are unique only within {outer}, but the model uses {inner} without {outer} and so treats units with the same label as one unit. Nest {inner} in {outer} in the formula.

movers_split.template: {count} units labelled by {inner} change their level of {outer}, and the model nests {inner} in {outer}, so it splits each of them into separate units. For outcomes measured on each occasion, use separate random terms for {outer} and {inner}, so that each unit keeps one random effect.

relation.template: In the design sample, '{first}' has {levels_first} labels and '{second}' has {levels_second}, which occur in {combinations} combinations. Relation from the labels: {relation}.

remedies.description: State the relation of the two units in the declaration, with nested_in, id_scope and membership, or as a crossing.
Write the random term with '/', as in (1 | school/class), so that the IR builds a grouping factor whose levels are unique across the data.
Use separate random terms for the two columns, with labels that are unique across the data, so that a unit keeps one random effect when it changes its parent.

combinations.definition: The number of distinct pairs of a label of the first column and a label of the second that occur together in a row of the design sample, which are the levels of the interaction of the two columns.

composite.definition: Whether some grouping factor of the IR is an interaction that contains both columns, such as the factor school:class of (1 | school/class) (ir.md, Random terms).

declared.definition: The relation that the declaration states for the two units whose only label column is one of the two columns. nested_within_parent, nested_global and nested_mobile apply when one of the units names the other in nested_in: with id_scope 'within_parent', with id_scope 'global' and membership 'fixed' or absent, and with id_scope 'global' and membership 'may_change_over_time' or 'multiple'. crossed applies when the crossings block lists the two units. none applies otherwise, including when there is no declaration.

first_in_several.definition: The number of labels of the first column that occur with more than one label of the second.

inner.definition: For a pair declared nested, the column that labels the unit that names the other in nested_in, and no column otherwise.

inner_in_several.definition: For a pair declared nested, the number of labels of the inner column that occur with more than one label of the outer column, and 0 otherwise.

levels_first.definition: The number of distinct labels of the first column in the design sample.

levels_second.definition: The number of distinct labels of the second column in the design sample.

outer.definition: For a pair declared nested, the column that labels the parent unit, and no column otherwise.

relation.definition: identical when first_in_several and second_in_several are both 0, first_nested_in_second when only first_in_several is 0, second_nested_in_first when only second_in_several is 0, crossed when combinations equals levels_first multiplied by levels_second and neither count is 0, and partially_crossed otherwise.

second_in_several.definition: The number of labels of the second column that occur with more than one label of the first.

entries.summary: Classifies how the labels of two grouping columns occur together in the design sample: as identical partitions, as one column nested in the other, fully crossed or partially crossed. It then compares the observed relation, and the way the IR combines the two columns into grouping factors, with the relation, ID scope and membership that the declaration states for the units the columns label. Labels that repeat under several outer units cannot show whether they denote one unit or several (02-decisions.md, Q4), so the check never recodes a column.
entries.title: Label incidence between grouping columns

rules.condition: status is between and slope_requested is true.
status is partially_within and slope_requested is true.

between_slope.template: As inferred from the data, '{term}' does not vary within any level of '{factor}', so a by-'{factor}' slope for it can only describe how the variance between levels changes with '{term}'. Its variance is not a slope variance and may not be identified. Remove the slope, or keep it only as a model of between-level variance.

partial_slope.template: As inferred from the data, '{term}' varies within {varying} of the {levels} levels of '{factor}' that have two or more rows, and in all its columns within {informative}, so its by-'{factor}' slope rests on those levels alone.

status.template: As inferred from the data, '{term}' is {status} with respect to '{factor}': it varies within {varying} of the {levels} levels that have two or more rows.

agreement.definition: The share of a level's rows that its most frequent row pattern must cover for the level to count as constant in the term.

sources.citation: 02-decisions.md, Q4. A rule that required 99% agreement within clusters recovered the school level in 99.3 to 100% of 2,000 replicates with up to 0.5% of rows miscoded.

references.citation: Review catalogue (docs/design/evidence/review-catalogue.md), L1-03, with the verifier's correction on coding and on the number of distinct values.

remedies.description: Remove the by-factor slope of a term that does not vary within the factor's levels, and model differences in variance between levels explicitly if they matter.

Separate the within-level and between-level parts of a numeric predictor: add its level means over the design sample and the deviations from them as columns declared with derived_from, and use both as predictors.

icc.definition: For a term with one column that is not coded from a factor, the ANOVA intraclass correlation of the column across the levels, (MSB - MSW) / (MSB + (n0 - 1) MSW), with MSB = SSB/(J - 1), MSW = SSW/(N - J), SSB the sum over levels of the level size times the squared difference between the level mean and the overall mean, SSW the sum of squared differences from the level means and n0 as structure.cluster_sizes defines it. It is absent for other terms, when J is 1, when N equals J or when the denominator is 0.

informative_levels.definition: The number of levels counted in varying_levels in which the rank by the sequential rule of the term's columns, restricted to the level's rows, after the level's first row is subtracted from every row, equals the number of columns of the term.

multi_row_levels.definition: The number of levels of the factor with at least two rows in the design sample.

slope_requested.definition: Whether a random term of the IR with this grouping factor has a term whose set of variables equals that of this fixed term, as estimands are matched with terms (declarations.md, estimands).

status.definition: between when varying_levels is 0, so that every level with at least two rows is constant in the term, within when varying_levels equals multi_row_levels and is above 0, and partially_within otherwise.

varying_levels.definition: The number of levels with at least two rows in which the term varies. A level is constant in the term when its most frequent row pattern, the values of the term's columns in a row compared exactly, covers at least the share agreement of its rows: with agreement written as m / 10^d, c rows of that pattern and n rows in the level, when c times 10^d is at least m times n in integer arithmetic. A level varies otherwise.

within_share.definition: For the same terms, SSW / (SSB + SSW), the share of the column's variation that lies within levels, absent when SSB + SSW is 0 or for other terms.

entries.summary: For each fixed term other than the intercept and each grouping factor, reports whether the term varies within the levels of the factor, how many levels inform a slope for it and, for a single numeric column, its intraclass correlation. Whether a term varies within a level is inferred with the tolerance of 02-decisions.md (Q4), so that a few miscoded rows do not turn a term that is constant within levels into one that varies, and the messages say that the status was inferred from the data. A by-factor slope for a term that does not vary within any level only describes how the variance between levels changes with the term. Whether such a variance is identified depends on the coding and on the number of distinct values, and it is never a slope variance.
entries.title: Within and between status of a fixed term

sources.citation: 02-decisions.md, Q5. The settings follow the confirmed defaults of the ACRO output-checking tool, with the dominance rule applied to the rows of a bin, and the maintainer adopted them on 8 November 2026. They are to be checked against the primary UK output-checking guidance before 1.0.
